Fit the discrete-time hazard model with fixed provider effects

Source: R/model_discrete_fe.R
fit_discrete_fe.Rd

Fits \(\mathrm{logit}\, h_{ijk} = \alpha_k + \gamma_i + Z_{ij}^\top\beta\), the hazard of the event in period \(k\) for subject \(j\) of provider \(i\), by maximum likelihood on one row per subject. The person-periods are looped over inside the computation and never stored.

Usage

fit_discrete_fe(
  data,
  max_iter = 10000,
  tol = 1e-05,
  bound = 10,
  backtrack = TRUE,
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data() with a survival outcome: time is the subject's last period (the event period, or the last period observed without the event) and event the event indicator. One row per subject, without start, weights or offset.

max_iter

maximum number of Newton iterations. Default 10,000.

tol

convergence tolerance on the period effects and covariate coefficients. Default 1e-5.

bound

provider effects are kept within median(gamma) +/- bound. Default 10.

backtrack

use a backtracking line search. Default TRUE.

message

print the iteration history.

Value

An object of class discrete_fe:

coefficients

a list with gamma (provider effects), alpha (period effects, named by period, the first fixed at zero) and beta (covariate coefficients).

linear_predictor

\(Z\hat\beta\) of the included subjects.

loglik, aic, bic

log-likelihood and information criteria (the BIC counts person-periods).

periods

the number of periods each subject is at risk.

time_grid

the event periods.

person_periods

the total number of person-periods at risk.

data, vars, sizes, cutoff, rows, control, converged

as for fit_logistic_fe(); rows counts subjects.

Details

The periods are the distinct values of time among the events: a period in which no subject has the event has a hazard of zero and adds nothing to the likelihood. A subject is at risk in every period up to its own time and has the event, if any, in its last one. The first period's effect is fixed at zero, so \(\gamma_i\) is the log-odds of the hazard in the first period at \(Z = 0\); tests and standardized measures do not depend on this choice.

The likelihood is that of the logistic model on the person-period data, and every result (coefficients, variances, tests, standardized measures) equals what fit_logistic_fe() gives on the expanded data with the period effects as covariates. The Newton step solves through the Schur complement of the diagonal provider block of the information, as SerBIN does.

See also

test.discrete_fe(), standardize.discrete_fe(), confint.discrete_fe(), summary.discrete_fe(), and var_select(model = "discrete") for selecting the covariates.

Examples

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, provider_size = c(20, 40), rows_per_patient = c(1, 1),
              type = "survival", seed = 1)
s$month <- pmin(ceiling(s$stop * 12), 12)
s$event[s$stop * 12 > 12] <- 0
pd <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
              time = "month", event = "event", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_discrete_fe(pd)
fit
#> Discrete-time hazard model with fixed provider effects
#>   599 subjects, 5355 person-periods, 20 providers, 12 event periods, 3 covariates
#>   log-likelihood -880.81; iterations 5
#>   provider effects: median -3.013, range -3.907 to -1.969
coef(fit)$alpha
#>            1            2            3            4            5            6 
#>  0.000000000 -0.425938274 -0.001920639  0.003559516  0.213482472 -0.055165573 
#>            7            8            9           10           11           12 
#>  0.065604829 -0.218351045 -0.558239003  0.050250679  0.053689440 -0.619540070
